info.name: 3PL Automation - Logic Apps
info.description:
Requests for the 6 Request-triggered Logic Apps (Standard) workflows in three3pllogicapp:
- onboarding-orchestrator (calls the other 5 via the native 'Invoke a workflow in this logic app' action)
- btp-config-publish
- mulesoft-config-generation
- mulesoft-config-publish
- solace-config-generation
- solace-config-publish

Each workflow has a single `When_a_HTTP_request_is_received` trigger. The 5 leaf workflows each call one local .NET function (see lib/custom/*/function.json) and return its output as the HTTP response body. `onboarding-orchestrator` doesn't call any function directly — it fans out to BTP/MuleSoft/Solace in parallel (each wrapped in its own Scope for isolated error reporting), chaining MuleSoft's and Solace's generate step output straight into their publish step, and joins on a single Response.

**Update-existing-config support:** mulesoft-config-generation and solace-config-generation can now auto-fetch a partner's current config file from GitHub (via the new FetchExistingConfigFile function) and merge this run's CSV-derived entries onto it (via GenerateMuleSoftConfig's existing updateExisting merge logic for MuleSoft, or the new MergeSolaceConfig function for Solace) instead of only ever building fresh. This is opt-in: supply repoOwner/repoName/branch/filePathPrefix (MuleSoft) or repoOwner/repoName/branch/filePath (Solace) in the request body; omit them and behavior is unchanged from before. See the 'MuleSoft Config Generation' and 'Solace Config Generation' request descriptions below for details.

**Local testing (default):** run the project with `func host start` (or F5 in VS Code with the Logic Apps Standard extension). The `baseUrl` collection variable defaults to `http://localhost:7071`, and no signature is required locally.

**Deployed/Azure testing:** set `baseUrl` to `https://<your-logic-app-name>.azurewebsites.net`, then enable the disabled `sv`/`sp`/`sig` query params on the request (values come from the workflow's Callback URL in the Azure Portal, or `az rest`/`az logicapp` callback-url APIs) since Standard Logic App HTTP triggers are SAS-signed when hosted in Azure.

Note: `githubToken` for the mulesoft/solace publish workflows and TriggerBtpDeployment's `githubToken` are both read from the `githubToken` app setting on the server side (`appsetting('githubToken')`), not from the request body, so they are intentionally omitted from these request bodies.

request.description:
Fans out to btp-config-publish, mulesoft-config-generation→mulesoft-config-publish, and solace-config-generation→solace-config-publish in parallel, each wrapped in its own Scope (Scope-BTP/Scope-MuleSoft/Scope-Solace) inside an outer Scope-Try/Scope-Catch. Do NOT send appYaml/devYaml/tstYaml/prodYaml under mulesoft.publish or solaceConfigJson under solace.publish — the orchestrator wires those in itself from the matching generate step's output (body('Invoke_MuleSoft_Config_Generation') / body('Invoke_Solace_Config_Generation')?['mergedConfigJson']). Only send the fields each generate/publish step actually needs from the caller (csvContent, repo/branch/path, commitMessage).

repoOwner/repoName/branch/filePathPrefix (mulesoft.generate) and repoOwner/repoName/branch/filePath (solace.generate) are optional but recommended: when supplied, each generate step auto-fetches its existing config from GitHub first and merges this run's entries onto it (MuleSoft via updateExisting=true; Solace always) instead of building from the CSV alone — so re-running the orchestrator for a partner that's already onboarded adds to their config instead of overwriting it. Omit them to build fresh, same as before this capability existed.

On success returns 200 with all 5 child outputs nested under btp/mulesoft/solace; on any child failure returns 500 with per-branch failure detail (result('Scope-Try') plus each domain's own result()).

Triggers a GitHub Actions workflow_dispatch (btp-Api-management-deploy.yml) via TriggerBtpDeployment. All body fields fall back to defaults baked into btp-config-publish/workflow.json if omitted; githubToken always comes from the server-side `githubToken` app setting.

request.description: Builds app/dev/tst/prod.yaml from a MuleSoft NAV onboarding requirements CSV (long format, one row per RowType: Environment/TransactionType/MessageType/SourceDestination/UomMapping). Set updateExisting=true to merge onto existing config instead of building fresh. As of the new Fetch_Existing_*_Yaml actions, you no longer have to paste the existing YAML in yourself: leave existingAppYaml/existingDevYaml/existingTstYaml/existingProdYaml blank and supply repoOwner/repoName/branch/filePathPrefix instead — the workflow auto-fetches each file from that branch first (via the new FetchExistingConfigFile function) and merges onto whatever it finds (blank/404 = nothing to merge against, same as a brand-new onboarding). filePathPrefix works with or without a trailing slash, same as the publish step. The existing*Yaml fields still work as a direct override if you'd rather not hit GitHub. See MuleSoftCsvParser.cs for the full CSV column reference.

request.description: Commits non-blank appYaml/devYaml/tstYaml/prodYaml content to a GitHub feature branch under filePathPrefix (creating the branch from baseBranch if needed). Normally chained after 'MuleSoft Config Generation' in the real pipeline, but can be called standalone for testing. githubToken is not accepted in the body here (Logic App reads it from the githubToken app setting).

Generates Solace onboarding config JSON from a CSV batch (multiple Brand/Env/SystemName/ThreePLCode records per call, unlike MuleSoft's single-record CSV). csvContent is required: solace-config-generation/workflow.json reads it straight from the trigger body with no hardcoded fallback, so an empty/missing csvContent will fail in GenerateSolaceConfig rather than silently falling back to a built-in sample.

repoOwner/repoName/branch/filePath are optional but unlock the new merge behavior: if supplied, the workflow fetches that file's current content from GitHub (via the new FetchExistingConfigFile function) and merges this run's generated entries onto it (via the new MergeSolaceConfig function) — upserting by name/aclProfileName/clientUsername/queueName per section, and unioning SUBSCRIPTION_LIST topics for a queue that's already subscribed, rather than overwriting the file. Omit them and the response is unchanged from before (fresh CSV-only build). The response body is now `{ generated: <raw GenerateSolaceConfig output>, mergedConfigJson: <string, ready to hand to Solace Config Publish> }` instead of the raw function output directly — use mergedConfigJson as the solaceConfigJson value for 'Solace Config Publish'.

Commits solaceConfigJson to a GitHub feature branch at filePath (creating the branch from baseBranch if needed). Normally chained after 'Solace Config Generation' — use that call's response `mergedConfigJson` field directly as solaceConfigJson here (it's already merged with whatever existed at filePath, if anything did) for an end-to-end test. githubToken is not accepted in the body here (Logic App reads it from the githubToken app setting).
